payload.claim: test_every_subnet_saffron_allocates_is_declared_in_one_place (tests/test_runtime.py:650) verifies 'draws from the declaration, not a second literal' two ways: a regex forbidding a quoted full CIDR string, and an equality check against runtime.SUBNETS. Both pass on a value that merely happens to equal the declaration without being derived from it: splitting the literal across two string pieces evades the regex (neither piece alone matches `"\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+/\d+"`) while the concatenated result still equals runtime.SUBNETS['egress'], so the equality assertion is unaffected. This is exactly the drift backlog item 143 exists to prevent: the day the declared subnet moves, this line silently keeps yesterday's value instead of tracking it, and no test in this diff would notice.
